autorally.create.hint: Pick the one squad that raises the banner to create a rally, and the Doom Elite level (1–35) the rally targets. Only one squad can lead; click it again to clear it.
autorally.drill.hint: Click a squad to change what it does: blank — stays home · ✓ — joins · 🚩 — leads (raises the banner). Only one squad can lead; clear the current one to move the banner.

autostart.enable: Check every hour and open the panel if it is not running
autostart.hint: A task in the Windows scheduler looks once an hour and opens the panel when it is not there — one panel, holding whichever profiles were open in it. It tells a working panel from a frozen one: an open panel notes the time every minute, and one that has stopped answering is closed and opened again. What it starts is this very install, under your own account.

autostart.state.profiles: One panel with the profiles that were open in it: {profiles}.
autostart.state.off: Not registered — nothing will open the panel by itself.
autostart.state.limited: The panel is running without administrator rights, so the task will open it without them too. Start the panel as administrator and tick this again to have it opened with them.
autostart.state.unsupported: The task scheduler is Windows-only — there is nothing to register here.

develop.hint: Both halves of a recording at once: a passive capture of the wire beside a tracer that wraps the client's own Lua. Switch it on, do the thing in the game ONCE, switch it off — then keep the pair with a description of what was done, or throw it away. A capture nobody labelled is a file nobody can read a week later. The tracer's hooks live in the running client, so Stop is asked politely and the panel puts them back if the child does not.

Goes into the log file name; spaces become underscores.

opt.autoloot_limit.hint: More than the daily budget makes no difference.
opt.autoloot_pause_min.hint: How long to wait once the day's robberies are gone.
opt.autoloot_poll.hint: How often the capture's checkpoint is re-read.
opt.daemon_port.hint: The panel picks it: one profile, one client, one port. Nothing to keep unique by hand.
opt.debug_send_url.hint: URL the debug-log archive is sent to. Empty — do not send. A stub for now — no transport is wired.
opt.game_exe.hint: The process name that means the game is running. Read off this machine — LW_GAME_EXE names another one.
opt.launcher.hint: Read off this machine — the ordinary install, or LW_LAUNCHER when the game lives somewhere else.
opt.log_max_lines.hint: How much the log widget keeps. panel.log is never trimmed.
opt.rdp_session: The game runs in another Windows session
opt.rdp_session.hint: Tick this for a second account: its client lives in a Windows session of its own (its own desktop), not on this one. The panel then looks for THAT client, and stops starting or restarting it from here — that would act on this desktop instead. The daemon port follows the tick — the panel hands out one nobody else uses.
opt.rdp_user.hint: The Windows user logged on to that session: the client is looked for among that user's processes. Empty means the same as unticked — the client on this desktop.
opt.sniff_ready_timeout.hint: How long to wait for both halves of a recording to report.
opt.sweep_dwell.hint: Below ~2 s the sweep outruns its own point — the map responses have not arrived yet.
opt.sweep_radius.hint: Half the side of the box around the centre.
opt.sweep_rest_min.hint: The map does not change fast enough to walk passes back to back.
opt.sweep_step.hint: Shorter than a screen: an extra jump is cheaper than a band of tiles nobody asked about.
opt.trace_filter.hint: Display filter for the panel log ONLY — the recording on disk always keeps every call. A substring of the Lua function name; «SFS» covers the whole wire. Widening it (e.g. «Manager», «Util») only shows more of what is already on disk, but tens of thousands of lines a second can still freeze the panel log — leave it narrow. Empty shows everything.
opt.watchdog: Relaunch the game when it dies
opt.watchdog.hint: Noticing the game process gone, start it again — at most once every 5 minutes.
opt.win_python.hint: It runs the captures, the robberies and the Lua daemon itself. Read off this machine — LW_WIN_PYTHON names another one.
panic.done: everything stopped; the schedule is off — switch it back on in the Timers tab
panic.log: stopping everything: monitors, watchers, the map sweep, the scenario and the schedule
profile.open_hint: Picking a profile that is not open opens it beside this one.
profile.client_shared: The profile «{others}» drives the same client as this one (daemon port {port}). The two take turns over one game, so each runs half as often as you set it and hears the other's traffic as its own. Give one of them a client of its own: «Profile» → «Separate the clients…».
profile.confirm_delete: Delete the profile «{name}»? Its whole directory {path} goes with it — the chat history, the rally and secret-task logs, panel.log and the record of when each timer last ran. This cannot be undone.
profile.error.empty_name: The profile name cannot be empty.
profile.error.last_one: This is the last profile — it cannot be deleted.
profile.error.no_login: Profile «{owner}» already drives the client on this desktop. This one needs the login of a Windows session of its own.
profile.error.no_port: No free daemon port: {first}–{last} are all taken.
profile.error.no_replacement: «{name}» is the only profile this window has open, and every other one is held by a second panel. Close that panel, or open another profile here first — deleting this one would leave the window with no page in it.
profile.error.not_removed: The profile directory {path} could not be removed: {error}. Something is still holding a file in it — a capture, a chat window, a log. «{name}» is still there and nothing has been changed.
profile.label: Profile:
profile.new.title: New profile
profile.new.login_hint: The client on this desktop already belongs to profile «{owner}». This profile gets a client of its own in a separate Windows session — type the login it signs in with. The panel picks the daemon port itself.
profile.new.console_hint: The client on this desktop is free, so this profile takes it. The panel picks the daemon port itself.
profile.new.bring_up: Raise the Windows session {user} now — the logon, the client and the daemon? It takes a few minutes and the log shows how it is going. «Bring the session up» on the «Game» page does the same thing later.
profile.separate.none: Every profile already drives a client of its own.
profile.separate.hint: These profiles drive the same client, so they farm one account. Type the Windows session login for each — the panel raises its client there and picks the port itself. An empty box leaves that profile as it is.
rally.no_squads: no squad is ticked — tick them in Settings → Auto Rally
rally_limit.frame: Daily rally caps by monster type
rally_limit.hint: How many rallies of each type auto-join may join per day. 0 = no cap. The count resets daily.
rally_tab.frame: Raise a rally on a world monster
rally_tab.hint: Each ticked squad raises its own rally on the chosen target of the chosen level, N times over. Levels run 1–200 for both targets — seasonal events put high-level monsters on the map — and a level the game has nothing for simply comes back empty. The «monster» daily cap (Settings → Auto Rally) is honoured. A repeat only counts once the game shows the new rally. The buttons beside the box are the levels rallied at most often — one press each. All four choices are kept in the profile and are back the next time the panel opens.
rally_tab.busy: waiting for another action to finish…
squads.title: Squads:

scenarios.empty: No action scripts found in src/lastwar_bot/actions/.
scenarios.hint: Select an action script and run it. Game-VM actions need the daemon; vision actions need the game window. Arguments are optional — {"squads": [2, 3]} — and a script that declares defaults runs without them.
scenarios.parse_error: does not parse: {error} — the file was NOT saved
scenarios.stopping: {name}: stopping — the run ends at its next step

secret.autoloot.rule_skip_own: · tiles on my own server are left alone

secret.autoloot.state.no_own: my own server could not be read — not robbing
secret.autoloot.state.no_login: the game is not logged in — nothing it says can be trusted
secret.hint: a passive sniff — move the map, or switch «Automatic map sweep» on
senddiag.empty: the debug log is empty yet
senddiag.title: Send diagnostics
senddiag.warning: No personal information is sent. The log contains only technical data about how the panel runs.
session.check.no_client: session {session} ({state}) is up, but no {exe} is running in it — «{button}» starts one there.
session.check.no_login: the box is ticked, but no login is typed — there is no session to look in.
session.check.no_session: nobody is logged on as {user} — «{up}» creates the session, starts the client in it and leaves it disconnected.
session.check.off: the box is not ticked: this profile's client is the one on this desktop.
session.check.probe_error: the session could not be read: {error}
session.check.unsupported: this Windows cannot be asked about its sessions (pywin32 is missing), so a client in {user}'s session cannot be found.
session.clash: the daemon port is {port} — this desktop's daemon. A profile looking into {user}'s session has to drive that session's daemon (47655 by default), or it reads one client and presses the buttons of another.
session.console_taken: Profile «{owner}» drives the client on this desktop. There is one desktop, so this profile stays in a Windows session of its own.
session.state.disconnected: disconnected — which is how it should be left
settings.tabs.hint: Which tabs this profile shows. A tab that is off is not built at all: no widgets, no settings page of its own, no triggers offered, and none of its captures or watchers started — «Secret Tasks» off is a capture and two watcher threads that never run. Untouched here, a tab follows the DEFAULT profile's own choice — switch it on or off there to reach every profile that has never set it for itself. The column beside each says what it brings up when it is on.
settings.tabs.restart: Saved. The list is applied the next time the panel starts — a tab brings up its own standing orders when it is built, and taking one down mid-flight is not the same thing.
sweep.no_centre: give the sweep a centre (X/Y) — there is nothing to walk without one
sweep.no_monitor: the secret-task monitor is off: there will be traffic and nobody reading it
sweep.rule: a {side}×{side} tile box · {jumps} jumps · ~{mins} min a pass
sweep.settings_hint: a {side}×{side} tile box — {jumps} jumps, ~{mins} min a pass
timers.editor.err_name: a name is needed — the schedule identifies the errand by it
timers.editor.err_steps: at least one step is needed
timers.editor.name: Name (id):
timers.editor.steps_hint: Steps, one per line. A line is either the name of an action script or DSL right here («TAP donate_1000 xall»). They run in order; a failed step abandons the rest, and the retry does the whole errand again.
timers.editor.title: Label in the list:
timers.hint: A ticked errand runs itself once its period has passed; the clock survives a restart — an hour that elapsed with the panel shut fires shortly after it opens. Nothing fires with the game closed; a failed run is not counted and is retried; two errands due at the same moment take their turn rather than going together. The list belongs to the profile: edit it with the buttons below — «⟳» re-reads the file if you edited it outside.
timers.log.already_running: {name}: already running — cannot be taken back, wait it out
timers.log.fire: {name}: {mins} min since the last run — starting
timers.log.not_queued: {name}: not queued — nothing to take off
timers.log.skip_busy: {name}: the panel is busy — staying in the queue
timers.log.skip_game: waiting for the game to start
timers.none_selected: pick an errand first — click its name
triggers.hint: A ticked trigger listens for its event on the wire and runs its scenario the moment it lands — a standing order, not a press. Nothing fires with the game closed; it shares the timers' one worker, so a trigger and a timer never run together. «⟳» re-reads the file.
triggers.log.died: {name}: the listener exited — no longer watching
triggers.log.backoff: {name}: kicked again — waiting {minutes} min before relaunching
triggers.log.poll_error: {name}: the check could not be read: {error}
triggers.log.no_squads: rally auto-join: no squads ticked on the «Auto Rally» page — nothing to send
triggers.log.rally_capped: rally auto-join: every rally type is at its daily cap — nothing joined
stats.empty: Nothing tracked yet — switch on «resource_tracker» in the Triggers list.
stats.hint: Filled by the «resource_tracker» trigger — switch it on in the Triggers list. Only increases are counted (what you took in); spends are ignored. A new day starts a new row; the history keeps.
tabx.no_game: no data — start the game and press Refresh
alliance.col.name: Name
alliance.hint: The roster with presence comes from the alliance ranking screen (al.rank); the panel cannot read it passively, so open that screen in the game, then press Refresh.
alliance.empty: no roster yet — open the alliance ranking screen and press Refresh
panel.busy.title: The profile is already open
panel.busy: A panel for profile «{profile}» is already open. Two panels on one profile write the same settings file over each other and drive the same daemon, so this one will not open. Use the window you already have — or start a panel on a different profile, which is perfectly fine.
inventory.empty: empty — press Refresh (needs the game running)
heroes.col.name: Name
heroes.empty: no heroes — press Refresh (needs the game running)
accounts.col.name: Character
accounts.empty: no characters — press Refresh (needs the game running)
accounts.hint: The characters on this account, as the server itself lists them — the same list the game's «Characters» screen shows, read without opening it. Level, power and the alliance tag come from the same answer. «Switch» does what tapping a character in the game does: the client logs out and comes back as it, which takes a few seconds.
accounts.confirm: Switch to {name} on server {server}? This disconnects the current session and reconnects as that character — anything the panel is doing right now stops with it.
secrettasks.hint: The STARRED alliance secret tasks, read live from the game, each with a countdown to when it becomes raidable. When the countdown hits zero the row lights up: the tile can be robbed, and with «Auto-loot ★» ticked it is robbed on its own. Switch on «secret_task_share» in the Triggers list to have a mate's share appear here too.
secrettasks.empty: no starred task — press Refresh (needs the game running)
secrettasks.alliance: Alliance secret tasks — who is running what
secrettasks.alliance.hint: The tasks the alliance has out right now: who dispatched each one, its rank, when it finishes and how many times it has been robbed. Read from the game when the tab opens and on «Refresh».
secrettasks.alliance.empty: nothing from the alliance yet — press Refresh (needs the game running)
secrettasks.click_hint: a click on the coordinate walks the camera there
secrettasks.collect_fail: collect not sent — daily limit spent or no game
secrettasks.ghost.hint: The squads of Ghost Ops. The game knows them all itself, so the list is read once when the tab opens and on «Refresh». The event runs one day a week — on the other six the table is empty and the line above says so. The robbery lives in «Command Post»; here you see what is out and can walk the camera to it.
secrettasks.ghost.allies: Ghost Ops — what the alliance has sent out
secrettasks.ghost.allies.hint: The squads your alliancemates have out in Ghost Ops right now: who sent it, its rank, where it landed, when it is back and how many times the tile has been robbed. It comes from the same single read as your own squads — the game keeps both lists — so «Refresh» fills the two pages at once. Robbing is on the «Командный пункт» tab.
secrettasks.ghost.allies.empty: nobody in the alliance has a squad out — press «Refresh» (the event runs one day a week)
cmdpost.no_game: nothing read — needs the daemon and a running game
cmdpost.ghost.title: Ghost Ops
cmdpost.ghost.hint: The squads of the weekly Ghost Ops — the game knows them all, so no map sweep is needed. A robbery is one message, no window and no march: the button shows only on the squads the game itself calls robbable. The event runs one day a week; on the other days the list is empty and every press is held. No live robbery has happened yet — the event was shut when this was written.
cmdpost.ghost.closed_empty: the event is shut today — nothing to rob
cmdpost.ghost.log_held: robbery held ({uuid}) — event shut, budget spent or no game
cmdpost.shared.title: Secret Mobile Squad
cmdpost.shared.hint: The secret tasks an alliancemate shares. Nothing is polled: the share arrives as a broadcast the moment someone presses it, so this page listens to the wire. Without «rob on sight» it only lists what it hears; with it, a mission matching the rule is robbed in a fraction of a second. The five-a-day budget is shared with every other secret-task robbery.
cmdpost.shared.empty: nobody has shared anything yet — tick «Listen» and wait
cmdpost.shared.log_on: listening — waiting for an alliancemate to share a secret task
cmdpost.shared.log_held: robbery held ({uuid}) — budget spent or no game
cmdpost.treasure.title: Hidden Treasures
cmdpost.treasure.hint: The chests an alliance's radar drops on the map. Nothing appears by itself: «Refresh» asks the server for the list, reads the answer and parks what came back — an empty list means there is nothing to dig right now. While a chest is being dug the chosen squad can join the dig; once it is dug, the reward can be taken. No live radar event has put a chest out yet, so both presses are built but unproven.
cmdpost.treasure.info: treasures the client knows: {n} · taken today — {daily}
cmdpost.treasure.empty: no treasure on the map — press «Refresh» (the radar event is not always on)
cmdpost.treasure.log_dig: a squad is on its way to dig ({uuid})
cmdpost.treasure.log_failed: not sent ({uuid}) — the treasure is gone, the day's limit is spent or the game is not running
cmdpost.treasure.log_no_squad: squad {squad} is not loaded — nobody to send digging
cmdpost.scan_on: listening to the map for {n}s — pan the camera (or tick «Automatic map sweep» on the Secret Tasks tab), or no tile will arrive
update.st.behind_dirty: an update is waiting ({behind}), but the working copy has uncommitted changes — commit or discard them
update.st.ahead: {ahead} local commit(s) ahead of origin — nothing to pull
update.st.diverged: the branch has diverged from origin (+{ahead} / -{behind}) — merge it by hand
update.st.offline: no route to origin — could not check
update.st.no_upstream: branch {branch} tracks no origin — nowhere to update from
update.st.detached: not on a branch (detached HEAD) — updating is off
update.st.not_a_repo: not a git checkout — updating is off
update.st.no_git: git not found — updating is off
update.confirm.title: Update
update.confirm.body:
Update the bot to origin/{branch} ({behind} commit(s), {remote})?

This is a fast-forward pull — no merge. The panel has to be restarted afterwards.
update.done.title: Updated
update.done.body:
Updated: {before} → {local}.

The panel is still running the old code — restart it with «Restart the panel».
update.fail.title: Not updated
update.fail.dirty: The working copy has uncommitted changes. Commit or discard them and try again — the update never overwrites anything by itself.
update.fail.diverged: The local branch has diverged from origin: a single pull cannot do it. Merge the branches by hand.
update.restart.title: Restart the panel
update.restart.body:
Restart the panel now?

The schedule, the monitors and any running scenario will be stopped. The game and the Lua daemon keep running.

web.hint: Open this address on a phone that is on the same network as this machine. The token is already in the link; if the phone cannot follow it, type the token in by hand.
web.warning: To reach it from outside the home network, forward this port on the router. The traffic is not encrypted, so the token is readable along the way — limit who may connect (an address filter on the router) or put it behind a VPN.
web.warning.tls: The traffic is encrypted by the certificate you named, so the token is not readable along the way. To reach it from outside the home network, forward this port on the router — and a self-signed certificate warns once on every device before it is remembered.
web.log.busy: port {port} is taken — another profile, or another program
web.log.token: new token made — every phone signed in with the old one is signed out

web.ui.login.hint: Type the token from the panel's «Web» tab.

web.ui.timers.head: Timers
web.ui.refused: busy — something else is driving the game
graphics.hint: The bot reads the game rather than watching it, so nobody has to look at this picture. On «Simplified» the client draws 10 frames a second at the lowest quality in a 640×480 window — measured at a fraction of a percent of the video card, against a quarter of it for a client left alone, and nothing the bot does gets slower. It applies at once, and it applies to THIS profile's client only, so the account playing in the background can be economising while the one you are watching is not. Half of it survives the game restarting and half does not: the window size comes back by itself, the frame rate and the quality do not — so after a crash or a restart, press it again.
graphics.state.idle: The client has not been asked yet — «Refresh» asks it.
graphics.state.now_vsync: now: quality {quality}, {width}×{height}; the frame rate is paced by the display, not by the cap ({fps}).
graphics.state.offline: the game is not running — «{mode}» is remembered and will be applied when you switch it with the client up.
graphics.state.unreadable: the client did not answer what it is drawing.
graphics.state.busy: something else is driving the game right now — try again in a moment.
graphics.state.lapsed: the game has restarted: the window is still {width}×{height}, but the frame rate and the quality are back to {fps}/s and {quality} — press «{mode}» again to put them back.
web.https: Optional: point those two at a certificate and its key and the panel serves HTTPS instead of HTTP. A self-signed one is fine — every device will warn once and remember. Make one with: openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 3650 -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -subj "/CN=panel"
web.ui.more.empty: This profile has no other screens.

log.session.save_hint: Windows will ask again after every reboot until the password is saved in Credential Manager. To save it once — in a terminal: tools\rdp_instance.py --user {user} --save-credential (Windows takes it; the panel never sees it).
